title: Position: static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky
learningObjectives: Explain position: static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky and apply the layout behaviour correctly.

understand.concept: The position property controls how an element is placed. static is normal positioning; relative keeps its normal-flow space and allows offsets; absolute is positioned relative to a containing block and removed from normal flow; fixed is positioned relative to a viewport or relevant containing block; sticky behaves like normal flow until a scroll threshold is reached.
understand.whyItMatters: Positioning affects containing blocks, overlap, and scroll behaviour. Absolute and fixed elements can cover content if space is not planned. Sticky positioning needs an appropriate scroll container and inset threshold.
understand.analogy: Positioning is like deciding whether a note stays in the document sequence, shifts slightly, floats over a section, or stays attached to a viewing area.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; the browser uses formal formatting, containing-block, and painting rules.

explain.narrative: The badge is positioned relative to the card because the card is positioned and establishes the containing block.

questions.prompt: Which position value removes an element from normal flow and positions it relative to its containing block?
questions.explanation: Absolutely positioned elements are removed from normal flow and use a containing block.
